Key Research Thinking Patterns: Pattern 1: Machine Learning for Force Reconstruction (Using pre-trained CNNs on synthetic data and fine-tuning on experimental data to achieve high accuracy in force reconstruction).

Pattern 2: Force Network Analysis (Constructing force networks using photoelastic particles and the G2 method, and analyzing them using persistent homology to understand the evolution of force networks in granular systems).

Pattern 3: Topological Data Analysis (Using persistent homology and the GUDHI Library to analyze the topological features of force networks and understand the changes in the networks during stick-slip dynamics).

Pattern 4: Experimental-Computational Hybrid Approach (Combining experimental data from photoelastic materials with computational methods such as simulations and machine learning to study the mechanical properties of granular systems)
Summary Description: Miroslav Kramar is a researcher specializing in the application of machine learning and computational methods to study the mechanical properties of granular systems and soft matter. His work focuses on force reconstruction, force network analysis, and topological data analysis using photoelastic materials and experimental-computational hybrid approaches. He has developed novel machine learning approaches to reconstruct forces in photoelastic materials and has analyzed the evolution of force networks in granular systems using persistent homology. His research has the potential to advance our understanding of the mechanical properties of granular systems and soft matter, and has implications for applications in materials science and mechanical engineering.
